text.p: Florida West International Airways, certified to fly last this week by the government, is confident its search for new investors will be successful, its president, Richard Haberly told Reuters.
"We will have no trouble finding investors," he said.
The Federal Aviation Administration certified the all-cargo carrier on December 2, Haberly said.
Florida West has been using wet-leased aircraft to fly to destinations in Latin America, he added.
The Department of Transportation(DOT) had earlier ordered Florida West to find a replacement for majority owner Mansour Rasnavid, an Iranian-born U.S. citizen, by August 1997, Haberly said.
He expected to begin serious discussions with potential investors after Christmas, when the busy season at Miami International Airport subsides.
"Some publicly-traded companies with significant amounts of money" have been among those interested, Haberly said.
Besides Rasnavid, another major investor in Florida West is a group of Chileans. They also control LanChile and all-cargo Fast Air. These Chileans own 24.9% of Florida West.
Florida West recently received DOT approval to fly twice weekly to Peru and will begin those flights in January, he said.

He also hopes to start flights to Europe -- in addition to those to Latin America -- using Lan and Fast Air planes as their newer and quieter aircraft meet Europe's recent noise rules. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
